Bad Implementation: Instant text swap inside button: `state.done ? 'Back to editor' : 'Open preview'`.
Good Implementation: `<Roll variant="fade">` wrapping label; old text departs as new enters.
Optical & CSS Principle: Continuous text identity; boundary clipping and alpha fade prevent jarring visual cuts.

Bad Implementation: Button scales to `.96` and changes background only after `a.click` finishes; no response during press.
Good Implementation: Button responds immediately on `state.pressed` with scale `.96` and background `#e4e4e4` before action resolves.
Optical & CSS Principle: Immediate kinetic acknowledgement of physical input precedes asynchronous resolution.

Lesson Title: A new row that jolts its neighbors
Bad Implementation: Note container uses `transition: none`, instantly pushing down "Standard shipping".
Good Implementation: `<Collapse reveal="drop">` with cubic-bezier transition on grid-template-rows carrying the row below.
Optical & CSS Principle: Spatial continuity; layout reflow must be animated continuously to prevent ocular saccade disruption.

Lesson Title: An icon that loses its identity
Bad Implementation: SVG icon is unmounted and re-mounted with a different path (`key={String(state.done)}`), flashing in place.
Good Implementation: Single persistent SVG stroke paths rotate 45° from `+` to `×` via CSS transition.
Optical & CSS Principle: Topological shape preservation; rotating identical strokes maintains element identity.

Lesson Title: A message that skips its exit
Bad Implementation: Toast unmounts on frame 0 when dismiss clicked (`state.phase !== 'change'`).
Good Implementation: Toast remains mounted for 320ms transition (`opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-4px)`).
Optical & CSS Principle: Asymmetrical lifecycle symmetry; arrivals and departures must both have visible kinetic transitions.

Lesson Title: A second choice restarts the motion
Bad Implementation: Highlight has `key={state.phase}`, forcing unmount/remount that restarts translate from 0px (Day).
Good Implementation: Highlight remains mounted with persistent key; CSS transition retargets smoothly from current coordinate.
Optical & CSS Principle: Monotonic interruptibility; interactive interruptions must branch from live state, not origin.

Lesson Title: An object jumps when it lands
Bad Implementation: `<Fly>` lands at destination rect of padded slot (`{...destination, x: slot.x, y: slot.y}`), jumping 4px inward.
Good Implementation: `<Fly>` lands exactly at destination avatar's own measured `rect()`, matching final geometry.
Optical & CSS Principle: Subpixel spatial registration; handoffs between coordinate systems must match physical pixel bounds.

Bad Implementation: Accumulated file rows clear instantly at loop boundary with no visible trigger.
Good Implementation: Pointer moves and clicks "Clear" button (`pressed: true`), explicitly causing the batch dismiss.
Optical & CSS Principle: Visual causality; state resets in continuous loops must be anchored to an observable cause.

Bad Implementation: Checked icon snaps into view, causing the adjacent "Design review" label to jump sideways abruptly.
Good Implementation: CSS variable `--tr-insert-progress` transitions width from 0 to 24px while check fades in smoothly.
Optical & CSS Principle: Eased spatial allocation; expanding containers must smoothly transport downstream inline siblings.

Lesson Title: A new row carries the list
Bad Implementation: New reviewer row has `transition-property: opacity` only; existing rows below jump instantly.
Good Implementation: `<Collapse reveal="drop">` animates height expansion, pushing existing rows down in lockstep.
Optical & CSS Principle: Fluid reflow; vertical insertions must ease height to preserve readability of neighboring content.

Lesson Title: A control carries the next action
Bad Implementation: First button expands instantly (`.ss-roll__mid { transition: none !important; }`), jolting "Settings".
Good Implementation: Button width transitions continuously via `<Roll variant="fade">`, smoothly gliding "Settings".
Optical & CSS Principle: Coordinated flex flow; sibling actions must glide continuously when adjacent buttons resize.

Lesson Title: A popup resizes with its content
Bad Implementation: Popup bounds snap instantly to 242x60px while content text is still fading in.
Good Implementation: Popup uses `--tr-surface-progress` to ease width and height synchronously with content opacity.
Optical & CSS Principle: Unified shell-content synchrony; bounding containers must resize concurrently with child content.

Bad Implementation: Grabbing file at right offset instantly translates file center to pointer (`translateX(24px)`).
Good Implementation: Pointer maintains exact grab offset from initial touch through travel and release.
Optical & CSS Principle: Rigid body dynamics; dragging must anchor rigidly to the initial contact point without snap.

Bad Implementation: Spinner appears static with `animation-delay: .35s`, freezing on screen before rotating.
Good Implementation: Spinner animation runs continuously before appearance; opacity fades in while already in rotation.
Optical & CSS Principle: Pre-warmed visual indicators; rotating loading states must be in active motion upon initial visibility.

Lesson Title: Text shifts as the transition finishes
Bad Implementation: Uses margin travel on overlapping inline-grid items, shifting the baseline of "Optional".
Good Implementation: Uses `<States>` with rigid baseline alignment and transform offsets, keeping baseline static.
Optical & CSS Principle: Baseline stability; changing labels must never perturb the vertical typographic baseline of sibling text.

Lesson Title: A label hits a hard edge
Bad Implementation: Label track translates vertically through a hard-clipped container, slicing letterform strokes.
Good Implementation: Container applies a vertical gradient mask (`linear-gradient(transparent, #000 6px, #000 calc(100% - 6px), transparent)`).
Optical & CSS Principle: Local edge feathering; moving typography must soften at boundaries while resting text stays sharp.

Bad Implementation: File list track scrolls past hard container edge with abrupt 1px clipping.
Good Implementation: Dynamic gradient mask activates on top/bottom edges (`--ed-top`, `--ed-bottom`) only while scrolled.
Optical & CSS Principle: State-driven edge disclosure; mask feathering should indicate concealed content only when scrolled.

Bad Implementation: All fields (currency, price, payment method, address) transition simultaneously on frame 0.
Good Implementation: Staggered offset: currency leads, followed by price, method, and address in overlapping waves.
Optical & CSS Principle: Multi-tier choreographic hierarchy; driving changes lead dependent updates in staggered tempo.

Bad Implementation: Tight margins (6px), export window jammed at top, status overlay covering active rows.
Good Implementation: Balanced 22px gutters, window bleeds off bottom, status chip placed in negative space.
Optical & CSS Principle: Negative space allocation; overlays must sit in quiet margins without occluding primary data.

Lesson Title: Make the UI read like a product
Bad Implementation: Chaotic layout, mismatched font sizes, competing buttons, no coherent columns.
Good Implementation: Clear title, muted metadata, fixed reading columns, and single primary action button.
Optical & CSS Principle: Typographic role differentiation; headers, metadata, and actions must occupy distinct roles.

Bad Implementation: Blue borders on every card, saturated badges, heavy drop shadows, colored text everywhere.
Good Implementation: Clean 1px neutral borders, subtle green badge, single dark action button, neutral text.
Optical & CSS Principle: Selective visual emphasis; container borders and shadows must recede so primary actions dominate.

Bad Implementation: Desktop 4-column data table scaled down via `transform: scale(.5)`, rendering 5px text.
Good Implementation: Table reflows into a 2-line stacked card layout with 12px text and inline metadata dots.
Optical & CSS Principle: Responsive content reflow; shrinking desktop layouts via scale transforms destroys legibility.

Bad Implementation: Confirmation card sits 1px away from panel edge, looking like an alignment bug.
Good Implementation: Confirmation card separated by deliberate 15px gap, making depth immediately clear.
Optical & CSS Principle: Near-tangent avoidance; adjacent edges must either align exactly or separate by `>= 8px`.

Bad Implementation: Container has 12px top padding but only 3px bottom padding; button crowds bottom edge.
Good Implementation: Uniform 12px padding around all four edges of outer and inner containers.
Optical & CSS Principle: Concentric uniform insets; padding must wrap completely around all perimeters evenly.

Lesson Title: Fit the contents of a control
Bad Implementation: Icons sit low in buttons due to mismatched line-height and unaligned flex items.
Good Implementation: Icons and text share an optically balanced flex row (`align-items: center; padding-block: 0`).
Optical & CSS Principle: Optical vertical alignment; icons and labels must center on the visible glyph, not line box.

Bad Implementation: Equal vertical gaps between every line; appointment titles float equidistant from times.
Good Implementation: Appointments grouped tightly with their metadata; distinct larger gaps separate groups.
Optical & CSS Principle: Gestalt proximity grouping; whitespace must bind related data and separate distinct records.

Bad Implementation: Low contrast gray card on tinted gray ground; faint text fails WCAG contrast.
Good Implementation: Crisp white card on tinted ground, dark readable text (`#444`), solid dark action button.
Optical & CSS Principle: Luminance step separation; foreground surfaces must establish a definite value step from ground.

Bad Implementation: Inbox is filled glyph, Folder is thin 1px outline, Archive is heavy 2.2px stroke.
Good Implementation: All icons share uniform 18x18px bounding box, outline style, and 1.5px stroke weight.
Optical & CSS Principle: Iconographic unity; icon sets must maintain identical stroke weights, styles, and optical volume.

Bad Implementation: Multi-color purple gradient ground, glowing bar charts, saturated purple typography.
Good Implementation: Clean white card, neutral 1px border, subtle gray bars with dark accent for active day.
Optical & CSS Principle: Signal-to-noise optimization; decorative gradients and glows must not drown functional metrics.

Lesson Title: Choose chrome that serves the task
Bad Implementation: Small sharing task forced into a desktop browser window with faux URL bar and tabs.
Good Implementation: Clean, dedicated sharing dialog card with focused document title, permissions, and copy button.
Optical & CSS Principle: Contextual container fidelity; modal tasks should not be forced into faux browser frames.

Lesson Title: Never push only the unread rows in
Bad Implementation: Unread rows add 8px left padding for their dot, causing the avatar column to zigzag.
Good Implementation: Every avatar aligns to a shared 0px column; unread dots hang in the left margin.
Optical & CSS Principle: Columnar alignment integrity; status indicators must never displace primary list alignment lanes.

Bad Implementation: Phone mockup sits directly over the dashboard's primary dollar revenue figure.
Good Implementation: Phone shifts to right margin, straddling edge, leaving both desktop and mobile amounts visible.
Optical & CSS Principle: Non-occlusion of narrative payoff; secondary device mockups must never cover primary metrics.

Lesson Title: Place a satellite around the story
Bad Implementation: Receipt card sits directly over export settings controls and primary Export button.
Good Implementation: Receipt card moves to bottom-right quiet margin, leaving export configuration visible.
Optical & CSS Principle: Satellite clearance; elevated satellite cards must float over inactive margins, not active forms.

Bad Implementation: 3 stacked windows all have identical high-contrast shadows and dark borders, fighting for focus.
Good Implementation: Supporting windows recede via muted gray fills and faint borders; active window leads.
Optical & CSS Principle: Depth plane hierarchy; background windows must recede tonally to elevate the foreground hero.

Lesson Title: Use the ground to frame the layers
Bad Implementation: Saturated orange ground with orange-tinted invoice and orange-tinted deposit card.
Good Implementation: Warm light cream ground (`#ebdac8`) frames crisp white cards with neutral charcoal text.
Optical & CSS Principle: Ground-to-figure contrast; warm backgrounds should frame neutral foreground surfaces, not tint them.

Bad Implementation: Dark workspace has gray preview document with identical dark slate borders, looking murky.
Good Implementation: Dark workspace hosts an authentic bright white document preview with crisp contrast.
Optical & CSS Principle: Multi-material authenticity; light documents inside dark workspaces must remain authentic white.

Lesson Title: Crop to the action and payoff
Bad Implementation: Entire library application scaled down to 62%, rendering text unreadable at 7px.
Good Implementation: Focused crop at 1:1 scale; sidebar is cropped off, keeping package title and action legible.
Optical & CSS Principle: Narrative crop priority; crop peripheral application navigation to preserve 1:1 text readability.

Lesson Title: Give the result the most weight
Bad Implementation: Uploaded file is a tiny 20px row lost in a dense list of 14 placeholder rows.
Good Implementation: List reduced to 8 spacious 38px rows; new file highlighted in blue tint with 500 weight.
Optical & CSS Principle: Focal hierarchy; newly introduced items must carry the greatest optical weight in the frame.

Bad Implementation: Window boundary slices right through the file size column ("4.2 MB" cut in half).
Good Implementation: Window width adjusted so the crop falls cleanly past the size column over empty margin.
Optical & CSS Principle: Clean crop boundary; crops must fall in whitespace or cut placeholder bars, never data words.

Bad Implementation: 4 equal 1/4 bento tiles, each displaying an identical heading and three gray skeleton bars.
Good Implementation: 1 tall hero tile with live document UI; 3 peripheral tiles show stat number, claim, and marks.
Optical & CSS Principle: Bento variety; identical repeated tile templates read as generic slop; one hero must dominate.

Lesson Title: Take the color from the product
Bad Implementation: Purple-to-pink gradient background, gradient text title, tinted cards, violet borders.
Good Implementation: Clean neutral background, solid dark title, crisp white card, green status only on live deploy.
Optical & CSS Principle: Anti-AI slop; avoid cliché violet/pink gradients and colored glowing borders.

Bad Implementation: Text shrunk to 8.5–10px to cram more metadata rows onto card, reading as wireframe.
Good Implementation: Legible 14px deploy titles, 12px metadata, fewer rows with generous breathing room.
Optical & CSS Principle: Minimum legible scale; avoid sub-11px typography in presentation mockups.

Bad Implementation: Every row displays branch, commit hash, author avatar, duration, and status badge.
Good Implementation: Only the focal active row displays full metadata; secondary rows display name and time only.
Optical & CSS Principle: Selective detail density; detailing every peripheral item overwhelms the core message.

Bad Implementation: Card, button, and icons emit neon indigo and cyan glowing drop-shadows.
Good Implementation: Single neutral shadow (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #0000000d, 0 6px 18px #0000000f`).
Optical & CSS Principle: Photometric realism; surfaces cast soft neutral shadows, not colored neon halos.

Bad Implementation: All-caps tracked typography on headings ("RECENT DEPLOYS"), buttons ("DEPLOY"), and rows.
Good Implementation: Natural sentence case ("Recent deploys", "Deploy") for high legibility and calm tone.
Optical & CSS Principle: Typographic casing hygiene; all-caps tracked labels slow reading and read as aggressive.

Lesson Title: Use an icon pack, not glyphs on fly
Bad Implementation: Hand-drawn SVG shapes in rainbow-colored squircle containers (purple, orange, pink).
Good Implementation: Unified Lucide icon set at 16px with consistent 1.75px stroke; color reserved for status.
Optical & CSS Principle: Standardized iconography; hand-drawn ad-hoc icons look amateur and break visual balance.

Lesson Title: Color icons with an opaque ink
Bad Implementation: Icons tinted with translucent RGBA/HEX (`#00000059`), creating dark intersections.
Good Implementation: Icons colored with 100% opaque solid ink tokens (`#9a9a9a`, `#1f9d55`, `#d1453b`).
Optical & CSS Principle: Stroke intersection rendering; translucent SVG strokes darken where lines cross (`onion skin`). (onion skin opaque ink stroke intersection)

Lesson Title: Name the AI action, don’t sparkle it
Bad Implementation: "Ask AI" button with gradient background, magic wand icon, and multiple sparkles.
Good Implementation: Clean neutral button with precise descriptive copy ("Explain failure") and quiet border.
Optical & CSS Principle: Semantic action naming; label AI features by their concrete utility, not magic sparkles.

Lesson Title: Throw a swipe at the finger’s speed
Bad Implementation: Row pauses at drag release (220ms delay), eases from rest, then gap snaps shut violently.
Good Implementation: Row maintains finger velocity on release, easing out smoothly while slot height closes in one ease.
Optical & CSS Principle: Kinetic momentum conservation; touch releases must preserve exit velocity without stutter.

Lesson Title: Draw a reaction as the app does
Bad Implementation: Hand-drawn white heart inside a solid red disc superimposed directly over message words.
Good Implementation: Real emoji inside a white pill anchored to the bubble's bottom-right corner, scaling in from corner.
Optical & CSS Principle: Platform reaction authenticism; reactions sit on bubble corners ringed in ground, scaling from corner.

Lesson Title: Draw a chart on from its start
Bad Implementation: Line chart, filled gradient area, and terminal dot all fade in simultaneously as a flat picture.
Good Implementation: Line draws left-to-right (`stroke-dashoffset`), area clip wipes underneath, end dot lands last.
Optical & CSS Principle: Progressive temporal reveal; trend data should draw sequentially to convey temporal directionality.

Bad Implementation: Top bar has an ellipsis button on the right, but the left side is completely empty and unpadded.
Good Implementation: Symmetrical top bar: Back chevron on the left, ellipsis on the right, balanced negative space.
Optical & CSS Principle: Navigation bar symmetry; top action bars must maintain bilateral balance or be omitted.

Bad Implementation: Extremely long name wraps awkwardly, email truncates with ellipsis inside chip.
Good Implementation: Realistic, well-proportioned names ("Jon Park", "Maya Chen") that fit allotted container tracks.
Optical & CSS Principle: Layout-matched mock copy; demo data must be curated to fit container constraints without truncation.

Lesson Title: Pin a changing label to its icon
Bad Implementation: Fixed 104px dropdown slot; label left-aligned, leaving variable gap before chevron.
Good Implementation: Label right-aligned against chevron; label grows leftward, keeping the 4px icon gap constant.
Optical & CSS Principle: Anchor preservation; dropdown labels must anchor against their disclosure chevrons.
